solution: Output width = floor((input - kernel) / stride) + 1. Layer 1: (32 - 5)/1 + 1 = 28, so 28 x 28. Pooling: (28 - 2)/2 + 1 = 14, so 14 x 14. Layer 3: floor((14 - 3)/2) + 1 = 5 + 1 = 6, so 6 x 6. (ii) With stride 2 the first output becomes floor(27/2) + 1 = 14 x 14: the feature map is about half the width (a quarter of the values), so less computation, but fine spatial detail can be lost because the kernel skips positions.

marking_points.criterion: Increasing stride reduces the output size (14 x 14) and computation but loses fine spatial detail.

acceptable_alternatives: Follow-through for later layers from an earlier error when the method is correct. For (ii) accept "smaller feature map" with either reduced computation or reduced detail.
partial_credit_notes: Award each independent point once, up to 4 marks. Accept equivalent correct wording or valid alternative code. Do not double-credit one idea.

verification.scope: Padding, channels/depth and parameter counts are not assessed. The size formula is stated in the reference, not required in the prompt.
